notes: One muse session and one claudecode session driven concurrently in the SAME cwd by run-cell-multi.sh, observed by a single --record daemon. The daemon labels each adapter independently (muse Process.Match=CommandPattern{muse-bin-...} + Source=FilesUnderRoot{~/.local/share/muse/sessions}, disjoint from claudecode's ExactName{claude} matcher and ~/.claude/projects root; muse's DiscoverPID additionally never reads its cwd argument, so cross-adapter mis-binding is structurally impossible, not merely avoided), so the workspace events.jsonl carries two distinct sessions — one per adapter — each with its own working->ready arc and no cross-contamination. This spec is adapter-agnostic: agentA is whichever session enters working first, agentB the other; both cells (muse + claudecode) share this expected.jsonl and the same workspace events.jsonl (each cell differs only in which transcript it stores for the replay golden). Every phase anchors on a WORKING transition, never a ready, because both adapters emit a pre-session proc-<PID> row born in ready that never works — anchoring on working skips those placeholders, and new_session on agentB skips agentA's already-matched session. Asserts: two distinct sessions, each an independent working->ready arc, in one workspace. SPEC CORRECTION (record, 2026-09-14, live recording session muse=01a0a136-61ef-7af3-9f05-8ca20ae0b3b9 / claudecode=cc8ef412-6e31-4a9d-aa87-eeccd3538f26): muse's session watch (agent.FilesUnderRoot over ~/.local/share/muse/sessions) is NOT cwd-scoped -- confirmed live: TWO ADDITIONAL, entirely unrelated top-level-looking sessions (f75b209e-4211-4719-9f37-18531eb084fe, e8a0649a-db15-469d-a545-403f369d8caf) appeared in this run's events.jsonl at delta+4.1s/+4.2s, both reaching their own ready by delta+9.9s -- these belong to OTHER, pre-existing muse-bin processes live on the recording machine at the time (unrelated to this recipe's driven cwd; confirmed absent from the driven $RUN_CWD and from this recipe's own muse session's subagent/ tree), not reminder children of our own session and not claudecode. Standard v4-UUID-shaped session ids give the validator NO structural way to tell such an alien muse session apart from a genuine second-adapter (claudecode) session -- recordedEvent (expected.go) carries no adapter field on state_transition events, and SessionIDPrefix cannot help either since muse's own top-level session ids are ULID-derived (time-of-day-dependent, not a stable literal across re-recordings) while claudecode's and muse's OWN reminder children's ids are both generic v4 UUIDs, visually and structurally identical. Without a correction, agentB_turn_start's bare new_session match latched onto the alien f75b209e session (delta+4.1s) instead of claudecode's real turn (delta+48.1s) -- a clean-looking 4/4 pass that measured the wrong session entirely, exactly the phantom-subagent failure mode this onboarding batch was warned about. Corrected with min_delay_ms:20000 on agentB_turn_start: the alien contamination window in this recording closed by delta+9.9s (10s of margin under the new floor) and claudecode's real turn didn't start until delta+48.1s (28s of margin above it) -- a pragmatic, evidence-based floor, not a structural guarantee against a future re-recording's differently-timed alien activity. The genuinely robust fix is a daemon/tooling change (surfacing an adapter tag onto events.jsonl's state_transition rows, or scoping muse's watch to the recipe's own cwd) -- out of scope for a spec-only correction; noted as a caveat, not filed as an issue. Every matched session in the PROMOTED recording was independently cross-checked directly against the raw daemon events and the driven $RUN_CWD/session-lock ownership before promotion.
